name: Ecosystem Reframing
consequences: Reframing Denmark's digital identity ecosystem as a resilience challenge rather than solely a privacy or ideology issue; this changes the framing of public sector risk, supplier concentration, reduced strategic autonomy, continuity-of-service exposure, and absence of robust fallback authentication path.
options: Position platform dependency as a national security concern
Highlight the economic benefits of digital sovereignty through increased procurement options and reduced vendor lock-in
Emphasize the democratic accountability implications of relying on foreign commercial platforms for critical public services
review: This lever introduces trade-offs between framing, advocacy, and policy engagement; it leaves unaddressed the challenge of securing buy-in from existing operators who may resist changes to their business model.

name: Technical Demonstrator Scope
consequences: Defining a scope for non-production technical demonstrators that is lean, defensible, and focused on secure, standards-based fallback-capable access models; this influences the project's credibility and ability to produce credible technical evidence.
options: Develop mobile-oriented demonstrators using open standards like FIDO2/WebAuthn and OpenID Connect
Explore browser-based or hardware-token-based fallback authentication paths that reduce dependence on mobile OS duopoly
Focus on a single, highly secure demonstrator that showcases the feasibility of platform-neutral access
review: This lever introduces trade-offs between technical demonstration and procurement influence; it leaves unaddressed the challenge of ensuring demonstrators align with future procurement requirements.

name: Procurement Language Influence
consequences: Influencing AltID-related design, policy, consultation, or procurement documents to include platform-neutrality, fallback access, continuity, resilience, or supplier-concentration language; this affects the project's ability to shape Denmark's digital identity infrastructure.
options: Seek inclusion of requirements stating that Danish digital identity systems should not depend exclusively on Apple or Google app stores
Advocate for a platform-neutral or certified fallback access path for critical public authentication
Push for procurement language that prioritizes supplier-neutrality and fallback-capable design
review: This lever introduces trade-offs between procurement influence and EU-level engagement; it leaves unaddressed the challenge of ensuring Denmark's advocacy aligns with broader European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and reduced platform lock-in.

name: EU-Level Engagement
consequences: Engaging with relevant EU bodies and technical working groups connected to the European Digital Identity Wallet framework; this affects the project's ability to shape Denmark's digital identity infrastructure in alignment with broader European requirements.
options: Align Danish advocacy with European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and reduced platform lock-in
Seek inclusion of language supporting platform-neutral access or certified fallback mechanisms in relevant European Digital Identity Wallet materials
Engage with EU bodies to influence the development of standards and procurement guidelines
review: This lever introduces trade-offs between EU-level engagement and procurement influence; it leaves unaddressed the challenge of ensuring Denmark's advocacy aligns with broader European requirements.

name: Project Team Composition
consequences: Assembling a project team that includes a lead researcher in mobile security, regulatory and compliance specialist, policy and public-affairs coordinator, technical lead for demonstrator work, and additional engineers or contractors; this affects the project's ability to produce credible technical evidence and engage with relevant stakeholders.
options: Ensure the technical staffing avoids dependence on a single specialist
Include experts in web authentication, hardware-token workflows, or Linux/GrapheneOS-related implementation
Recruit team members experienced in Danish digital governance and procurement processes
review: This lever introduces trade-offs between project team composition and budget allocation; it leaves unaddressed the challenge of securing sufficient funding for institutional overhead, external security review, and limited legal/procurement support.

name: Physical Location and Institutional Overhead
consequences: Securing a physical base in Copenhagen with access-controlled workspace appropriate for security-sensitive digital identity research, development, and stakeholder meetings; this affects the project's ability to engage with relevant stakeholders and produce credible technical evidence.
options: Choose a location at a Danish university, independent research institution, or security-qualified R&D facility
Budget explicitly for institutional overhead, external security review, and limited legal/procurement support
Ensure the physical location is equipped to handle sensitive digital identity research
review: This lever introduces trade-offs between physical location and budget allocation; it leaves unaddressed the challenge of securing sufficient funding for project operations.

name: Success Criteria
consequences: Defining success criteria that include a published feasibility and risk report, delivered non-production technical demonstrators, formal written response from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen or another relevant authority, and inclusion of platform-neutrality language in official AltID-related documents; this affects the project's ability to demonstrate its impact and influence Denmark's digital identity infrastructure.
options: Focus on producing credible technical evidence through demonstrator development
Prioritize securing formal written responses from relevant authorities
Emphasize the inclusion of platform-neutrality language in official documents
review: This lever introduces trade-offs between success criteria and project scope; it leaves unaddressed the challenge of ensuring the project's EU-level engagement contributes to broader European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and reduced platform lock-in.

name: Digital Identity Governance Framework
consequences: Establishing a platform-neutral fallback authentication path will require revisiting Denmark's eIDAS implementation to ensure compliance with the new requirements.
options: Embed platform-neutrality directly into the eIDAS framework as an explicit requirement for all digital identity providers in Denmark.
Create a separate governance framework that prioritizes platform neutrality and fallback capabilities, potentially conflicting with existing eIDAS implementation.
Develop a hybrid approach where platform-neutral components are integrated into the existing eIDAS infrastructure on a case-by-case basis.
review: The primary trade-off is between maintaining existing eIDAS compliance and introducing new governance structures that prioritize platform neutrality. The gap left unaddressed is how to ensure seamless integration of platform-neutral features with the existing eIDAS framework without compromising overall digital identity security.

name: Public-Private Partnership Model
consequences: Engaging in a public-private partnership will require significant coordination and resource allocation from both government and private sector entities.
options: Develop a joint public-private working group to identify areas of collaboration and resource sharing for platform-neutral digital identity initiatives.
Create a separate, industry-led organization that drives the development of platform-neutral digital identity standards and best practices.
Establish a public-private partnership where the government provides funding and resources in exchange for private sector expertise and investment in platform-neutral digital identity solutions.
review: The primary trade-off is between leveraging public-private partnerships to accelerate platform-neutral digital identity initiatives and maintaining control over sensitive government information. The gap left unaddressed is how to ensure effective collaboration and resource sharing between public and private sectors without compromising national security interests.

name: Digital Identity Standards Harmonization
consequences: Harmonizing digital identity standards across Denmark will require significant investment in education and awareness-raising efforts among industry stakeholders.
options: Develop a comprehensive set of digital identity standards that are aligned with international best practices and prioritize platform neutrality.
Create a certification program for digital identity providers that meet the new, harmonized standards.
Establish a working group to coordinate the development of digital identity standards across Denmark's public sector institutions.
review: The primary trade-off is between investing in education and awareness-raising efforts to promote digital identity standardization and ensuring effective implementation across diverse industry stakeholders. The gap left unaddressed is how to ensure seamless integration of harmonized digital identity standards with existing eIDAS implementation without compromising overall digital identity security.

name: Regulatory Sandbox Environment
consequences: Establishing a regulatory sandbox environment will require significant investment in infrastructure and personnel to support experimentation and innovation.
options: Create a dedicated regulatory sandbox where industry stakeholders can experiment with platform-neutral digital identity solutions without fear of regulatory reprisal.
Develop a phased approach to regulatory sandbox implementation, starting with small-scale pilots and gradually scaling up to larger, more complex experiments.
Establish a public-private partnership to fund and support the development of a regulatory sandbox environment for platform-neutral digital identity initiatives.
review: The primary trade-off is between investing in infrastructure and personnel to support experimentation and innovation within a regulatory sandbox environment and ensuring effective oversight and regulation. The gap left unaddressed is how to balance the need for experimentation with the requirement for robust regulation and oversight.

name: Digital Identity Education and Awareness
consequences: Investing in digital identity education and awareness-raising efforts will require significant investment in resources and personnel.
options: Develop a comprehensive digital identity education program that targets industry stakeholders, policymakers, and the general public.
Create a certification program for digital identity professionals that emphasizes platform neutrality and fallback capabilities.
Establish a working group to coordinate digital identity education and awareness-raising efforts across Denmark's public sector institutions.
review: The primary trade-off is between investing in digital identity education and awareness-raising efforts and ensuring effective implementation across diverse industry stakeholders. The gap left unaddressed is how to ensure seamless integration of harmonized digital identity standards with existing eIDAS implementation without compromising overall digital identity security.

name: Platform-Neutral Digital Identity Incubator
consequences: Establishing a platform-neutral digital identity incubator will require significant investment in resources and personnel to support innovation and experimentation.
options: Create a dedicated platform-neutral digital identity incubator where industry stakeholders can develop and test innovative solutions without fear of regulatory reprisal.
Develop a phased approach to incubator implementation, starting with small-scale pilots and gradually scaling up to larger, more complex experiments.
Establish a public-private partnership to fund and support the development of a platform-neutral digital identity incubator.
review: The primary trade-off is between investing in infrastructure and personnel to support innovation and experimentation within an incubator environment and ensuring effective oversight and regulation. The gap left unaddressed is how to balance the need for experimentation with the requirement for robust regulation and oversight.

name: Digital Identity Community Engagement
consequences: Engaging with the digital identity community will require significant investment in resources and personnel to support outreach and education efforts.
options: Develop a comprehensive digital identity community engagement program that targets industry stakeholders, policymakers, and the general public.
Create a certification program for digital identity professionals that emphasizes platform neutrality and fallback capabilities.
Establish a working group to coordinate digital identity community engagement across Denmark's public sector institutions.
review: The primary trade-off is between investing in digital identity community engagement efforts and ensuring effective implementation across diverse industry stakeholders. The gap left unaddressed is how to ensure seamless integration of harmonized digital identity standards with existing eIDAS implementation without compromising overall digital identity security.

name: Denmark's Digital Identity Infrastructure Review
consequences: Conducting a thorough review of Denmark's current digital identity infrastructure will reveal the complexity and depth of the country's dependence on foreign technology suppliers. This review is essential to understand the scope of the problem and identify potential solutions.
options: Conduct a comprehensive analysis of MitID, AltID, and other relevant digital identity systems in Denmark
Engage with international experts to assess the global best practices for digital identity infrastructure development
Develop a detailed inventory of all digital identity-related contracts, agreements, and partnerships within Denmark
review: A thorough review would expose the intricate web of dependencies between MitID, AltID, and other systems, revealing the lack of a clear fallback path in case of platform changes or outages. However, it might overlook the impact of existing power dynamics among stakeholders on the feasibility of proposed solutions.
